verdicts.trueWording: the novel is a failure, shadowy and inconclusive
verdicts.note: eNotes live 403; read via Wayback raw capture 20250317060057id_. Quote is verbatim in the review's penultimate sentence, prefaced 'But all in all'. Page citation confirms F&SF Vol. 40, No. 4, April 1971, p. 69, reprinted in CLC. Russ adds that such books are usually called 'promising' and predicts Wolfe will rise far above Ares.

verdicts.trueWording: not the baroque weirdness of its textures
verdicts.note: eNotes live 403; read via Wayback raw 20250316194237id_. Verbatim in the third body paragraph: it is 'this very familiarity', not the baroque weirdness of its textures, that makes Sword of the Lictor so powerful. Referent note: the familiarity is immediately explained by Wolfe never losing sight of his sources and mythical resonances, and by his words sounding like forgotten friends, so the claim's 'familiarity of Wolfe's sources' is a fair but glossed reading. Page has 'its textures'; claim says 'his'. Citation: Fantasy Newsletter Vol. 4 No. 12, Dec 1981, pp. 16-17, 32.

verdicts.trueWording: neologisms mingle with resurrected antique words
verdicts.note: Same Wayback capture. Verbatim in the second body paragraph (marked p. 16 territory, before the '(pp. 16-17)' marker), describing Wolfe's 'language of startling alienness'. Page continues 'and chimerical hybridizations of Latin, Greek, Germanic roots' - the claim drops 'chimerical' but is otherwise exact.

verdicts.trueWording: may have seemed picaresque, somewhat random in nature
verdicts.note: eNotes live 403; read via Wayback raw 20241005181348id_. Verbatim in the paragraph following the '(pp. 1-2)' marker. Two context points: 'the first three volumes' is the CLC editor's bracketed gloss (page reads Severian's [experiences in the three volumes preceding The Citadel of the Autarch]), and Clute's sentence ends 'though colorful enough' before he insists nothing in the narrative is accidental. Source is Book World - The Washington Post, January 30, 1983.

verdicts.trueWording: It was a very hard read, the plots did not link
verdicts.note: Live sffworld page fetched with a browser UA (HTTP 200). Post #1, article post-55366, author Belgarion, datetime 2002-09-25T13:29:12+0100 - matches the cited date. Quote verbatim; the sentence continues 'very well' plus a typo'd clause about looking like a short collection of stories.

verdicts.trueWording: was basically a collection of short stories
verdicts.note: Same live page and same post #1 (post-55366, Belgarion, 2002-09-25). Verbatim in the sentence naming the quartet The Book of the New Sun, which continues 'even though the whole plot was based around Severian in Chronicle Order'.

verdicts.trueWording: I had the feeling that I missed a lot
verdicts.note: Same live page. Post #13, article post-55425, author 'fortytwo', 2002-09-25T18:24:54+0100 - post number, handle and date all match. Verbatim; the sentence opens 'It's quite a while since I read the series and it held my interest, but'. The poster's gender is not stated on the page (the claim's 'his' is an assumption); he/she adds an intention to re-read.

verdicts.trueWording: the style is one of the key selling-points
verdicts.note: Same live page. Post #16, article post-55509, author jfclark, 2002-09-25T22:53:29+0100 - all three match. Verbatim (page hyphenates 'selling-points'), and the immediately preceding sentence is the concession that Wolfe's style in these books could turn some readers off.

verdicts.trueWording: I don't think I would recommend this book even to someone
verdicts.note: Live eyrie.org fetch, HTTP 200. Verbatim as the opening sentence of the final paragraph, which continues 'who read the original series'. Footer reads 'Reviewed: 2004-09-10', matching the cited date; rating 5 out of 10. One qualification the claim omits: the paragraph ends with an exception - read it if you are going on to an analysis such as Borski's Solar Labyrinth.

verdicts.trueWording: not sure that this series quite lived up to the promise
verdicts.note: Live eyrie.org fetch, HTTP 200. Verbatim in the final substantive paragraph, opening 'In the end, I'm not sure...' and continuing 'of its beginning'. Footer 'Reviewed: 2004-06-28' matches the cited date. The same sentence balances it with 'but at the same time it didn't entirely let it down', so the verdict is mixed rather than negative.

verdicts.trueWording: people who don't seem to understand what's going on yet declare
verdicts.note: Live blogspot fetch, HTTP 200. Verbatim in the opening paragraph (curly apostrophes as quoted), in the sentence beginning 'Half of the reviews of The Book of the New Sun are'. Byline Brian Murphy, dated March 29, 2025, post title 'Gene Wolfe is intimidating. The Knight is not. I also recommend smoked brisket.' Page has 'are people who'; the claim's 'are by people who' is a grammatical smoothing. Murphy's one-word reaction is 'Weird.'

verdicts.trueWording: being dense, labyrinthine, and outright incomprehensible at times
verdicts.note: Live tachy.org fetch, HTTP 200. Verbatim in the third body paragraph. Precise page framing: the book 'doesn't seem to be discussed much outside of a few enclaves of hardcore SF/F readers, probably due to its reputation of' being dense etc. So the attribution is hedged ('probably') and is about how little the book is discussed outside a hardcore-reader niche; 'narrow readership' is a close paraphrase of that, not the page's own noun.

Same live tachy.org page, same third paragraph, sentence beginning 'Characters are often'. Verbatim, and the reviewer is reporting others' descriptions rather than his own view - the paragraph after it says his own experience was overwhelmingly positive. Same sentence also reports the plot being called a straightforward hero's journey.

verdicts.trueWording: so neat it *ought* to be true. But it can't be.
verdicts.note: lists.urth.net timed out on the live fetch (curl 28, twice); read via Wayback raw capture 20210416053644id_. Verbatim, asterisks included, in the first paragraph of Lackey's own text, directly under the quoted claim that 'We're given another explanation for the missing guard in the BOOK OF THE SHORT SUN' - so the cross-book reading is exactly what he rejects. Header: Roy C. Lackey, Tue Sep 5 12:52:16 PDT 2006, thread '(urth) Close reading: Torturer chapter I'. He refutes it on seasons: swimming weather versus the icy winter of Triskele and Valeria.
